corpusName: Local KJV Corpus (Phase 6 Local KJV Corpus Completion)
translation: King James Version (1769 Blayney standard text)
publicDomainStatus: The King James Version text itself is public domain worldwide (originally published 1611; no live copyright claim blocks reuse outside the UK, and even the UK Crown-copyright administrative arrangement does not restrict this kind of reuse).

packagedSource.author: M2K Developments / All Bible
packagedSource.vendoredReason: Vendored as static JSON data under data/kjv-corpus/raw rather than an npm runtime dependency, so the exact corpus content is version-pinned, auditable in-repo, and immune to upstream package changes.

importedDuring: Phase 6 — Biblical Knowledge Completion (Local KJV Corpus Completion)

validation.canonicalBookOrder: Genesis (1) through Revelation (66), matching services/scriptureReferenceNormalizer.js book-name conventions
validation.checksumMethod: SHA-256 of each file under data/kjv-corpus/raw (sorted by path), then SHA-256 of the concatenated per-file digests. Recomputed by scripts/alpha/localKjvCorpusValidation.js on every run and compared against this recorded value to detect silent corpus drift.

markupNotes.FI_tags: <FI>...<Fi> marks KJV translators' italicized supplied words (words not in the original-language text, added by the 1611/1769 translators for English readability). Preserved as plain text by the normalizer (italics metadata is not currently surfaced to callers).
markupNotes.RF_tags: <RF>...<Rf> marks KJV marginal/alternate-reading footnotes (e.g. literal Hebrew/Greek renderings). Stripped from the primary verse text by the normalizer; not currently exposed as structured data.
markupNotes.CM_tag: <CM> marks a paragraph break in the original KJV printing. Stripped from plain text output.

provider.wiredInto: services/bibleTextProvider.js (Tier 1 — highest-priority provider, ahead of the configured approved provider and the bible-api.com external fallback)
provider.externalProviderRetained: services/canonicalScriptureProvider.js (bible-api.com) remains Tier 3 fallback, used only if a reference cannot be resolved locally (e.g. a malformed or non-canonical reference) or if the local corpus module itself fails to load.
